brief: Te Wera was a Ngā Puhi chief from the north who settled at Māhia on the East Coast, creating peace with his former enemies there and providing a mantle of protection and solidarity throughout a large part of Ngāti Kahungunu. Because of the peace and order he introduced, hospitality towards missionaries became possible. By the time of his death in 1839 an indigenous Māori Christian mission was growing within the kinship networks of the area.
